LESSON MENU
JUMP INSTRUCTIONSLE
In the 8086 microprocessor, jump instructions alter values in the instruction pointer.
DISCUSSION
By altering the IP register, the address of the next instruction is controlled differently than normal.
Jump instructions are used to change the flow of a program.
They can also return program flow and subroutines.
For example, your computer may require that it service inputs.
MAIN PROGRAM
SUBROUTINE
A subroutine is used to eliminate writing steps every time a service is required...
The main program jumps to the subroutine and back each time the main program is instructed to service the input.
Since the input service program is only written once the Jump instruction saves valuable memory space.
This is important in a program because a subroutine can be executed hundreds of times....
What register is altered in the 8086 microprocessor for Jump instructions?
Jump instructions do not alter the accumulator. Jump instructions are used to direct the flow of a program.
TRY AGAIN!
The Program Counter is found in the 8080/8085 microprocessor.
TRY AGAIN!
There are two general categories of Jump instructions......
Let's discuss the Unconditional Jump first..
Unconditional Jump instructions cause a jump every time they are executed...
These jumps do not alter any registers except the IP, nor do they alter the Flag register...
In the 8086 microprocessor, the address contained in the opcode instruction is NOT an actual address.
A DISPLACEMENT is used to locate the new address...........
The displacement indicates the number of memory locations between the contents of the Instruction Pointer at the jump location and the new memory location.
For example, this program would normally flow from location 1000 to1001, 1002, 1003, and 1004.
A Jump instruction causes the flow to go from 1000 to 1004.
The instruction pointer initially contained the address of the next instruction, 1001.
The Unconditional Jump instruction changed the IP to 1004.m
The address used in the JMP instruction is 03. This is the displacement or number of memory locations between 1001 and 1004.
The 8086 jump instruction operates as follows:.............

Note that if the microprocessor is required to jump backwards to an instruction, the displacement value must be subtracted from the current IP location. This is accomplished by 2's complimenting the displacement....
In this case the displacement is 05, from 1005 (contents of IP) to 1000.
Taking the 2's complement of 05 produces FB. The JMP FB instruction causes the IP to decrement 5 memory positions.
Taking the 2's complement of 05 produces FB. This Jump instruction is JMP FB.
Definition
Now let's look at Conditional Jumps........................
Conditional Jump instructions only cause a jump if a particular condition is met.
XX is a variable for the particular condition.
Address is the new location of the next instruction.
If the condition is not met the IP is incremented in the normal manner...
In the 8086 microprocessor, the address is the displacement.
The Conditional Jump instructions use the Flag register to determine if a particular condition has been met.
STATUS FLAGS
O - OVERFLOW
CONTROL FLAGS
D - DIRECTION
I - INTERRUPT
AC - AUXILIARY CARRY
There are numerous Jump instructions, let's look at some typical ones...

This instruction examines the logic condition (1 or 0) of the zero flag and will cause the program to jump when the zero flag is reset (0). If the zero flag is set (1), the program will continue with normal program flow.
This instruction examines the logic condition (1 or 0) of the zero flag and will cause the program to jump when the zero flag is
set (1). If the zero flag is reset (0), no jump occurs.
This instruction examines the carry flag and jumps if the carry flag is reset (0). When the carry flag is set (1), no jump occurs.
This instruction examines the carry flag and jumps if the carry flag is set (1). When the carry flag is reset (0), no jump occurs. )
This instruction examines the parity flag and will jump if the parity flag is reset (0). When the parity flag is set (1), no jump occurs.
This instruction examines the parity flag and will jump if the parity flag is set (1). If the parity flag is reset (0), no jump occurs.
What is the displacement using an 8086 microprocessor if the jump instruction is at 2005, the IP is at 2008, and jump location is 200E?
Remember the displacement is from the location of the IP register to the new location. A displacement of 09 is from the location of the jump instruction to the new location.
TRY AGAIN!

Remember the displacement of jumping ahead is positive and jumping back is a negative 2's complement. You found the displacement for jumping back and you should have found the displacement for jumping ahead...
TRY AGAIN!
What kind of conditional jump is JZ?
The jump (if not zero) is the JNZ instruction, not the JZ instruction.
TRY AGAIN!
The jump (if carry) is the JC instruction not the JZ instruction.
TRY AGAIN!
